html:
A large phosphate deposit in the interior of Western Sahara, found in 1947 and mined from 1972, with a conveyor belt of about 100 km carrying the rock to the coast near Laayoune, one of the longest in the world.

Phosphate is used for fertiliser, and Bou Craa made Spanish Sahara worth holding just as Spain faced calls to leave. After the Green March and the Madrid Accords of 1975, Morocco's state phosphate company took it over. The Polisario Front attacked the belt in the war, and today campaigners for Sahrawi independence call the exports plunder. Morocco already held the world's largest phosphate reserves. See also Morocco.
